import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    corr_threshold = 0.6
    correlated_groups = []
    
    # Build correlation matrix
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    
    # Find correlated pairs
    used = set()
    for i in range(len(feats.ids)):
        if i in used:
            continue
        group = [feats.ids[i]]
        used.add(i)
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= corr_threshold:
                group.append(feats.ids[j])
                used.add(j)
        correlated_groups.append(group)
    
    # Select one representative from each group
    representative_ids = [group[0] for group in correlated_groups]
    
    # Filter to relevant features
    relevant_indices = [feats.column(fid) for fid in representative_ids]
    relevant_x = feats.x[:, relevant_indices]
    
    # Calculate mutual information for all features
    mi_scores = mutual_info_classif(relevant_x, feats.y)
    
    # Sort by MI score and select top 3 features
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(mi_scores)[::-1][:3]
    selected_features = [representative_ids[i] for i in sorted_indices]
    
    # Use top 2 features as drivers (limit to prevent too many terms)
    drivers = tuple(selected_features[:2])
    
    # Check for interaction terms among top features
    products = []
    if len(drivers) >= 2:
        # Add interaction between first two drivers
        products = [tuple(sorted([drivers[0], drivers[1]]))]
    
    # Create columns list with all representative features
    columns = tuple(representative_ids)
    
    # Simple loading weights (equal for all features)
    loadings = {fid: 1.0 for fid in representative_ids}
    
    return Design(
        drivers=drivers,
        columns=columns,
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
